Article Title: 'Even Mughals called Shivaji a chuha': Uddhav likens Gen Z to Maratha warrior
Article Text:
Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray likened Gen Z to Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj

Shiv Sena (UBT) chief Uddhav Thackeray on Wednesday likened Gen Z to Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj , saying that even Mughals had called the Maratha warrior a "chuha" (rat), just as the current generation is being called "cockroaches".Addressing a gathering during a book launch in Mumbai, Thackeray said those who had been dismissed as "cockroaches" belonged to Generation Z, roughly between the ages of 13 and 28 and drew a parallel how Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj was only 17 when he captured Torna Fort, while Sant Dnyaneshwar was also very young when he wrote the Dnyaneshwari."Those who were insulted as 'cockroaches' belong to what we now call Generation Z roughly from the ages of thirteen or fourteen to twenty-seven or twenty-eight. Wasn't Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj just about that age when he captured Torna Fort at seventeen? Even Shivaji Maharaj was called a 'Chuha' by Mughal. Wasn't Sant Dnyaneshwar also very young when he wrote the Dnyaneshwari? Both faced tremendous opposition in their own time," Thackeray said.He said Shivaji Maharaj had challenged the Mughal Empire despite his young age, arguing that today's youth should not be belittled for speaking out.This comes at a time when political leaders across party lines have increasingly adopted Gen Z terminology to sharpen their political messaging during the ongoing Monsoon Session of Parliament.From treasury bench members defending the Centre's reforms to opposition MPs criticising the government's handling of the NEET controversy, lawmakers turned to internet slang more commonly associated with social media than parliamentary debate.BJP MP Bansuri Swaraj invoked Gen Z slang while backing the proposed legislation, using the phrase "clock it", a popular internet expression used to acknowledge or recognise something.Speaking in support of the Bill, she said, "Borrowing Gen Z's language, I would have to say that Modiji clocked it at providing this legislative solution."On the other hand, Congress MP Priyanka Gandhi Vadra invoked Gen Z terminology while criticising Prime Minister Narendra Modi's public outreach, arguing that young people were able to see through political messaging."If you want to win over the Gen Z, then making videos with different camera angles will not help. The prime minister needs to change the angle of his heart, not the angle of cameras," Priyanka said."Injustice has been done with youths under your government, accept the truth. Prime Minister Narendra Modi must take responsibility," she added.
Article Summary: Shiv sena (ubt) chief uddhav thackeray likened gen z to chhatrapati shivaji maharaj. He said that even mughals had called the maratha warrior a "chuha" (rat), just as the current generation is being called "cockroaches" this comes at a time when political leaders across party lines have increasingly adopted gen z terminology.

Article Title: ADGCA-ordered probe cleared Dreamliner fuel switch: Government
Article Text:
Test found no abnormality in dreamliner fuel switch

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: A DGCA-ordered probe by Boeing into the fuel control switch locking mechanism of the B787 Dreamliner has found “no abnormality”, govt told Parliament on Wednesday.The regulator had ordered this repeat examination after the crew operating an AI Dreamliner from London to Bengaluru in Feb had observed an issue with the switch after landing safely and had reported the same.The switches, which control fuel supply to engines, have been under scrutiny after AI 171 crashed within seconds of taking off from Ahmedabad in June 2025 as its engines had run out of fuel. While the incident is still being probed, the locking system of fuel control switches has been probed multiple times since then to ensure safety.Dreamliners operating around the world are still being looked at by the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB), which is probing the crash. The Dreamliner is the most widely used mid-range wide body aircraft globally.“DGCA, as part of continued airworthiness, directed original equipment manufacturer (OEM) level testing of fuel control switch locking mechanism in Seattle. Detailed examination of fuel control switch including structural integrity of fuel control switch detents was carried out and no abnormality was observed,” minister of state for civil aviation Murlidhar Mohol said in reply to a Parliament question Wednesday.The minister, however, added that “further inspection of complete thrust control module at OEM facility is underway”.This module translates pilot inputs or autothrottle commands into precise electronic signals to control engine power.On Feb 2, 2026, the AI Dreamliner on which the crew had reported an issue with the fuel control switch after landing in Bengaluru had been grounded for checks. At that time, AI had said in a statement: “We are aware that one of our pilots has reported a possible defect on the fuel control switch of a Boeing 787 aircraft...We have grounded the said aircraft and are involving the OEM to get the pilot’s concerns checked on a priority basis. The matter has been communicated to the aviation regulator, DGCA. Air India had checked the fuel control switches on all Boeing 787 aircraft in its fleet after a directive from the DGCA, and had found no issues.”On the AI 171 crash, Mohol said Wednesday: “There is no delay in the investigation. The timeline for a major accident investigation cannot be predicted, as it depends on several factors and is an evolving process. The final report will be made public and published on AAIB’s website after completion.”
Article Summary: Test found no abnormality in dreamliner fuel switch locking mechanism. The regulator had ordered this repeat examination after the crew operating an ai dreamliner from london to bengaluru in feb had observed an issue with the switch. The switches, which control fuel supply to engines, have been under scrutiny after ai 171 crashed within seconds of taking off from ahmedabad.

Article Title: India Stack goes global: DigiLocker work starts in Kenya, Cuba
Article Text: NEW DELHI: India has signed agreements with 24 countries to export its digital public infrastructure model, moving beyond broad cooperation pledges to begin work on DigiLocker systems in Kenya and Cuba and expand UPI-linked payments across 10 overseas markets. Discussions are also underway with Laos, Seychelles, Venezuela, Armenia, Fiji, Guyana and Colombia for possible adoption of platforms such as e-Sanjeevani, e-Office and e-Hospital.The electronics and information technology ministry told Lok Sabha on Wednesday that India had concluded an implementation framework agreement and a non-disclosure agreement with Kenya for deploying DigiLocker. Development of a foundational DigiLocker platform has also begun in Cuba.The agreements provide for capacity building, exchange of technical knowledge and best practices, expert consultations, joint workshops, feasibility studies and pilot projects. The partner countries include Kenya, Cuba, Colombia, Sri Lanka, Brazil, Maldives, Mongolia, Seychelles, Armenia, Fiji, Venezuela, Ethiopia and Tanzania.The overseas push seeks to position India Stack — the ecosystem of interoperable identity, payments, document and service-delivery platforms — as a development tool, particularly for countries in the Global South.India conducted a specialised course on digital public infrastructure for a Cuban delegation in December 2025 under the Indian Technical and Economic Cooperation programme. Foreign delegations from Kenya, Rwanda, Nepal, Indonesia and South Africa have also interacted with agencies such as UIDAI, NPCI, the National Informatics Centre and C-DAC.UPI merchant payments are currently available in Bhutan, France, Mauritius, Nepal, Qatar, Singapore, Sri Lanka, the UAE and Cambodia. Cross-border person-to-person payment links are operational with Singapore, Nepal and Greece.Among the latest additions, UPI merchant payments went live in Cambodia in June 2026, while a person-to-person link with Greece became operational in May. Nepal introduced cross-border person-to-person transfers in June, adding to merchant payments available there since March 2024.The government has also approved a Social Impact Fund to provide financial and technical assistance for pilot deployment of digital public infrastructure in low- and middle-income countries.
Article Summary: India has signed agreements with 24 countries to export its digital public infrastructure model. Discussions are also underway with laos, seychelles, venezuela, armenia, fiji, guyana and colombia. The overseas push seeks to position india stack as a development tool, particularly for countries in the global south.

NEW DELHI:These are the words of 69-year old Union minister Jitendra SIngh, who was addressing the Lok Sabha on Wednesday.Until recently, these words belonged to Instagram comment sections, meme pages, K-pop fan communities and WhatsApp chats. This week, however, they echoed through the halls of Parliament.During the Monsoon session, MPs infused their speeches with Gen Z slang and internet catchphrases while taking on political rivals, discussing governance and framing arguments around issues ranging from education to development.BJP MP Bansuri Swaraj, while defending the Centre's policies, urged the Opposition to "" — a Gen Z phrase meaning to recognise or acknowledge something. "Where Congress created a policy vacuum, Modi clocked it, if I may borrow the language of Gen Z, and created a solution. All the Opposition did was chase political opportunism," she said, explicitly acknowledging that she was borrowing from the vocabulary of younger generations.BJP’s Tejasvi Surya reached for another popular internet expression, calling the Opposition "" — shorthand for "delusional" — suggesting its criticism of the government was detached from reality.Not to be left behind, Congress MP Deepender Hooda, during debate on anti-paper leak in Lok Sabha, slipped in ‘’ and viral internet catchphrase “” in a swipe at Centre. “(Today is my birthday, so please resign cutie pie)," he remarked, giving example of slogans at the recent student protests.Meanwhile, Shiv Sena MP Shrikant Eknath Shinde labelled the Opposition as suffering from "" — the "Fear of Missing Out" — and even described it as "" (Missing in Action), implying that the Opposition was scrambling to remain politically relevant after missing key opportunities.It was an unusual moment.As Hooda put it, the GenZ with Bhagat Singh’s slogan of ‘Inquilab Zindabad’, turned it into ‘Vastaguna huiya’ when they protested against the government.Parliament, traditionally associated with constitutional language, Hindi idioms and literary references, suddenly sounded like an Instagram comment thread.The internet has a way of making words travel across continents, cultures and generations. Many expressions that now dominate Gen Z conversations were born in niche online communities long before they entered mainstream discourse.Unlike many internet expressions, "clock it" has a much older cultural lineage. The phrase traces its roots to African-American and LGBTQ+ ballroom culture in the United States, where "to clock" someone meant to notice, identify or call out something—often a flaw or inconsistency.Popularised through drag culture and shows such as, the expression later migrated to TikTok and Instagram, where Gen Z adopted it to mean "spot the truth" or "call it as it is".The phrase traces its roots to the viral meme "Can I get a Hoya?", in which a teenager shouted the line in an exaggerated tone. In India, content creators gave the meme a local twist by replacing the original phrase with the nonsensical-sounding "Vasteguna Huiya".The humour lay not in the words themselves—they have no literal meaning—but in the confused reactions they elicited. From there, the phrase spread rapidly across Instagram memes, reels and comment sections before making its way into the CJP student protests."Kuchu Puchu" does not have a single, traceable origin like "delulu" or "FOMO". Instead, it evolved organically from baby talk, a simplified, affectionate style of speech used by parents, grandparents and couples across many Indian languages.The phrase is believed to be a playful variation of words like "kuchi kuchi," "guchu puchu," "kuchi poo," and similar rhyming expressions that mimic the sounds babies make. Such reduplicative words are common in Hindi, Bengali, Tamil and several other Indian languages, where they are used as terms of endearment for children, pets or romantic partners.In recent years, "kuchu puchu" was revived and popularised by Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts and meme pages, where it took on a new, often sarcastic meaning. Calling someone "kuchu puchu" can imply that they are overly pampered, babied, innocent or treated with excessive affection.Its popularity surged during the CJP-led student protests, where protesters and social media users used "kuchu puchu" satirically to poke fun at political leaders and institutions.Unlike most Gen Z slang, FOMO predates social media. The acronym, standing for "Fear of Missing Out", entered popular vocabulary in the early 2000s as psychologists and marketers described the anxiety people felt when they believed others were enjoying experiences they were not part of.Instagram amplified the phenomenon, turning FOMO into one of the defining emotions of the social media age. Today, the term is used far beyond personal life—to describe everything from investment trends to political strategy.Originally a military abbreviation for "Missing in Action", MIA has been repurposed by internet users to describe people who suddenly disappear from conversations, social media or public life.Perhaps the most recognisable Gen Z word today, "delulu" is a shortened version of "delusional". It first gained popularity within K-pop fandoms, where devoted fans jokingly described unrealistic fantasies—such as believing their favourite idol secretly loved them—as being "delulu".Over time, the term evolved beyond fandom culture to describe anyone perceived as wildly optimistic or disconnected from reality. Today, it has become a staple of political banter, where opponents routinely accuse each other of being "delulu".The timing of Parliament's linguistic makeover is not accidental.The recent protests spearheaded by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) over NEET examination paper leaks were organised as much on Instagram and X as they were on the streets. Protesters used memes, short-form videos, viral hashtags and internet humour to mobilise students and simplify complex issues around examination reforms.For many young Indians, politics is now consumed through Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts and meme pages rather than lengthy parliamentary speeches or television debates. Viral clips often carry more influence than hour-long discussions.Taking notice of the same after massive protests, Prime Minister Narendra Modi also advised his Cabinet to engage with the youth on Instagram through reels and interactive sessions. "Young people are just on Instagram. This is a potential segment of citizens that we all need to connect with," he said.India's demographic profile makes this shift even more significant. With one of the world's youngest populations and millions of first-time voters entering the electorate every election cycle, speaking the language of youth has become a political strategy as much as a communication style.Although Gen Z slangs in Parliament may sound dramatic, Parliament has always reflected the language of its times.In the early decades after Independence, speeches frequently quoted verses from the, couplets by poets like Mirza Ghalib, Allama Iqbal. Hindi literary works were seen as a mark of oratorical skill.Long before MPs began saying "delulu" or "clock it", Parliament had embraced the language of popular culture. Bollywood dialogues have long been used to simplify political arguments, inject humour and produce memorable sound bites.Rahul Gandhi's dig at GST by calling it "Gabbar Singh Tax" transformed a complex debate on GST into a phrase instantly understood across India, while Prime Minister Narendra Modi invoked the character "Mausi" from the Sholay to mock the Congress party during his address in Parliament on July 2, 2024. He teased the opposition over their electoral defeat by mimicking a dialogue: "" (Oh Mausi, we have lost for the third time too, but it's a moral victory, right?).In another instance, BJP MP Kangana Ranaut brought DDLJ’s iconic dialogue ‘’ to life while addressing women’s reservation bill in Lok Sabha.Cricket metaphors soon followed, with terms like "hitting a six", "playing on the back foot" or being "clean bowled" by the Opposition. Finance ministers have described Budgets as "innings", while election victories and defeats have routinely been framed as cricket matches.In many ways, Gen Z slang is simply the latest chapter in this evolution. Parliament has never existed in a linguistic vacuum; it has always absorbed the language spoken beyond its walls.Every generation believes the next one's vocabulary sounds strange.Words like "cool", "awesome", "dude" and "LOL" were once dismissed as youthful fads before becoming mainstream. Today's internet lexicon follows the same trajectory.Many Gen Z expressions have travelled remarkable distances—from Korean pop fandoms to American drag culture, from gaming communities to TikTok trends—before landing in Indian political discourse. Their journey illustrates how digital platforms have accelerated the movement of language across borders and cultures.Not every slang term will survive. Internet vocabulary evolves at dizzying speed, with new words replacing old ones every few months. But some expressions inevitably escape their online origins to become part of everyday speech.When lawmakers adopt them, it signals that these words have crossed into the mainstream.When Bansuri Swaraj paused to say, "if I may borrow the language of Gen Z", she acknowledged something larger than a passing linguistic trend.Politics is no longer communicated solely through ideological speeches or parliamentary rhetoric. It increasingly competes in the same digital ecosystem as influencers, meme pages and viral videos, where relatability often matters as much as reasoned argument.Whether that makes parliamentary debate more accessible or more performative remains open to debate. But one thing is clear: as India's politics becomes increasingly digital, the House is learning to speak not just to Gen Z, but increasingly like Gen Z.
Article Summary: Parliament has always borrowed popular language from the internet. This week, mps infused their speeches with gen z slang and internet catchphrases while taking on political rivals. Many expressions that now dominate gen z conversations were born in niche online communities long before they entered mainstream discourse.

What the government said about the AI-171 probe

NEW DELHI: The Centre on Wednesday said no abnormality has been found in the fuel control switch locking mechanism of the Air India Boeing 787 Dreamliner that crashed shortly after take-off from Ahmedabad on June 12 last year killing 260 people on board and on the ground.Civil aviation state minister Murlidhar Mohol informed the Rajya Sabha that the fuel control switch was examined at the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) level in Seattle as part of continued airworthiness checks ordered by the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA), Reuters repeorted.A detailed examination of the fuel control switch, including the structural integrity of its locking detents, found 'no abnormality', Mohol said in his response to questions raised by Congress MP Jebi Mather Hisham. However, the examination of the complete thrust control module is still underway at the OEM facility in Seattle."Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA), as part of continued airworthiness, directed Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) level testing of Fuel Control Switch Locking Mechanism in Seattle. Detailed examination of Fuel Control Switch including structural integrity of Fuel Control Switch detents was carried out and no abnormality was observed.However, further inspection of complete 'Thrust Control Module' at OEM facility is underway," Mohol write in his written reply.The government also rejected suggestions that the Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) has delayed its final report into the crash.In her Rajya Sabha question, Mather had asked the government to state the reasons for the delay in releasing the final report more than a year after the crash, whether pilot conduct was among the factors being examined and whether the government would announce a public release date for the complete report.Responding to these questions, Mohol said there was 'no delay' in the investigation and explained that major accident investigations cannot be completed according to a fixed timeline."There is no delay in the investigation. The timeline for a major accident investigation cannot be predicted, as it depends on several factors and is an evolving process involving multiple variables," he said in the written reply.The minister said the investigation remains under way and that all possible causes and contributing factors are being examined."All probable causes and contributing factors leading to the accident are being investigated," Mohol said.The government said the final investigation report, containing all the findings of the probe, would be made public and published on the AAIB website once the investigation is complete.Air India flight AI-171, which was headed to London, crashed shortly after taking off from Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel International Airport in Ahmedabad on June 12, 2025.The Boeing 787 struck a medical college hostel complex soon after take-off. The crash killed 241 people on board and 19 people on the ground, while one passenger survived.The disaster became one of India's deadliest aviation accidents in recent years and triggered a detailed investigation into the circumstances surrounding the crash.A preliminary investigation report released last year found that the fuel control switches of both engines moved from 'RUN' to 'CUTOFF' shortly after take-off, cutting the fuel supply and causing both engines to shut down.A cockpit recording also captured a brief exchange between the pilots in which one pilot appeared to ask the other why the switches had been moved, while the other denied doing so. The finding raised questions about whether the switches had been moved by a pilot or whether a technical issue could have been responsible.The government has not provided a specific date for publication of the final AAIB report.Mohol said the investigation was still progressing and that the report would be released only after the inquiry is completed. The government has maintained that the investigation will cover all probable causes and contributing factors.
Article Summary: 'no abnormality found in fuel control switch': government on air india boeing 787 crash. Civil aviation state minister murlidhar mohol informed the rajya sabha. The crash killed 241 people on board and 19 people on the ground, while one passenger survived.

Article Title: Candace Owens drops unseen Charlie Kirk video, Alex Jones claims assassination story is ‘100% dead’

Alex Jones says Candace Owens’ video raises fresh questions about Tyler Robinson

What Candace Owens claimed after releasing the Charlie Kirk rooftop footage

Owens argued that the man in the video does not match Tyler Robinson, who was arrested after the shooting and accused by authorities of carrying out the attack. Soon after the footage was released, Alex Jones publicly backed her claims, saying the “official narrative” had “collapsed.” The video has now added fresh attention to a case that is still moving through the courts. A judge has not yet decided whether Robinson will stand trial.After Candace Owens shared the rooftop footage on July 28, Alex Jones reposted it and strongly supported her claims. He argued that the clip appeared to be “raw and unedited” and questioned whether it matched the version of events presented by investigators.Jones wrote:“The Official Charlie Kirk assassination story is now 100% dead! This is the same footage that the court will not let the public see, that we are meant to believe is Tyler Robinson assassinating Charlie Kirk.”He then compared the person seen in the video with Robinson and claimed they did not appear to be the same individual.“The individual does not look like Tyler Robinson. The rifle is never pulled from his pants. The person in the footage has no limp. Nowhere do we see the shooter assembling the gun on the roof as we were told. No recoil is seen. He performs military maneuvers with precision as well as signaling before opening fire. The official narrative just COLLAPSED…”Earlier this month, surveillance footage shown during Robinson’s preliminary hearing appeared to show a man walking across the Utah Valley University campus with what prosecutors described as a limp before the shooting.Candace Owens has repeatedly questioned whether Tyler Robinson was responsible for Charlie Kirk’s killing. She raised similar doubts in a previous interview with CNN journalist Elle Reeve and repeated those claims during the latest episode of her podcast, where she played the newly released video.While explaining the footage, Owens said the man on the rooftop carried out what she described as a military-style movement.“Now what happens next is exactly as my source stipulated. Now the rooftop guy begins a tactical crawl that is actually known in the military as a lateral crawl. We are not sure what that flash is. Um actually this looks like, oh, I’m not going to read into it. There’s that throw forward. I say fold forward. You can say throw forward, but that’s definitely something being flung forward, getting into position. ”Authorities have continued to identify Tyler Robinson as the accused in the case. Article Title: Three firefighters killed as deadly wildfires rage across southern Europe
Article Text:
The wildfires now stretch across a vast area from the Atlantic coast.

Three firefighters died while battling fast-moving wildfires in Greece as an intense heatwave continues to fuel blazes across large parts of southern Europe, forcing hundreds of thousands of people from their homes and stretching emergency services.Greece's fire department said the firefighters lost their lives while tackling separate fires on the island of Crete and in the country's southern mainland. The deaths came as soaring temperatures and strong winds made firefighting operations increasingly difficult.The wildfires now stretch across a vast area from the Atlantic coast to the eastern Mediterranean, affecting countries including France, Spain, Greece and Turkey. Fire experts have expressed concern over the number of large blazes burning close to populated areas, warning that many remain difficult to contain.France recorded temperatures of 38C in Bordeaux on Wednesday, where firefighters prevented a major forest fire from spreading into nearby suburbs. In Spain, temperatures reached 37C in Madrid as authorities reported progress in containing the country's largest wildfire on record.Spanish Interior Minister Fernando Grande-Marlaska said the blaze west of Madrid had been "technically stabilised", although emergency crews continued working to eliminate remaining hotspots.Emergency services said dozens of firefighting teams managed to contain the Madrid-area fire overnight. However, another wildfire near València remained out of control despite relatively cooler temperatures of around 32C.Speaking from the Navalcarnero emergency command centre, Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said conditions around Madrid were improving but warned that the coming hours would remain critical."I believe the next 12 hours will be very important," Sánchez said. "They are going to be decisive in consolidating the work done by the national civil protection system."He also noted that the Madrid wildfire had become the first in Spain's history to be raised to "operational level 3", requiring the national government to assume responsibility for managing the emergency.Authorities across western Europe said the latest heatwave, the region's fourth this summer, has significantly increased the risk of wildfires. High temperatures combined with powerful winds have made existing fires harder to extinguish while raising the possibility of previously controlled blazes reigniting.Fresh fires also prompted new evacuations in parts of Greece and Turkey.In France, officials said calm weather overnight had allowed firefighters to quickly deal with flare-ups. However, authorities warned that changing weather conditions could make firefighting more difficult in the coming days.The Gironde prefecture said 126 firefighters had been injured since the wildfire began, although the total area burned remained unchanged at about 42,000 hectares on Wednesday morning.According to data from the European Forest Fire Information System, France has recorded its largest area burned by wildfires, while both France and Spain have experienced an unusually high number of fires for this stage of the year.More than 330,000 people across southern Europe have been forced to leave their homes or hotels because of the fires.As conditions improved in some areas, officials lifted evacuation orders around Bordeaux, Madrid and València, allowing many residents to return. Some found their homes damaged or destroyed, with buildings reduced to burnt shells and personal belongings charred by the flames.The European Union has expanded support for countries battling the fires. Earlier this week, the European Commission deployed seven aircraft and four helicopters to France from several member states, including Sweden and Turkey.Spain also received international assistance, with six firefighting aircraft from Greece, Italy and Turkey, along with 134 personnel and 41 vehicles from Portugal. A Super Puma helicopter from Serbia was expected to arrive in Madrid on Wednesday, followed by another 40 emergency personnel and 18 vehicles.The European Union's crisis management authorities warned that the wildfire season is far from over and said they expect further outbreaks in countries such as Italy and Greece in the coming weeks as extreme summer conditions persist.
Article Summary: Greece's fire department said the firefighters lost their lives while tackling separate fires on the island of crete and in the country's southern mainland. The deaths came as soaring temperatures and strong winds made firefighting operations increasingly difficult.

Article Title: Russia launches overnight ballistic missile attack on Ukraine, killing 13
Article Text:
Photo credit: Reuters

Ukraine expands strikes on Russia's logistics network

Russia launched a wave of overnight air strikes across Ukraine on Thursday, killing at least 13 people, including one in Kyiv. In the attacks that reached as far as the western city of Lviv, prompted neighbouring Poland to scramble fighter jets to secure its airspace.Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko warned about the ballistic missiles heading towards the capital and urged residents to take shelter. Explosions were then heard in Kyiv, according to a Reuters witness. In the western city of Lviv, local officials said two apartment buildings were damaged and six people were injured.The attacks also inflicted heavy casualties elsewhere in the country. Six people, including two children, were killed in the Dnipropetrovsk and Poltava regions, while in Zelenskyy's hometown of Kryvyi Rih, six more people lost their lives after what local officials said was a direct strike by a Russian Iskander-M ballistic missile.Among those killed in Kryvyi Rih were two girls aged 5 and 12. Eight other people were injured in the strike. Oleksandr Vilkul, head of the city's defence council, said the missile was launched from Russia's Voronezh region and hit the home of a large family. Describing it as "a dark night", he warned that the death toll could rise as emergency workers continued clearing the rubble.In the western city of Lviv, near the Polish border, rescue workers searched through the debris after Russian missiles damaged two apartment buildings and injured 15 people, according to local officials.Earlier, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy had warned that Russia was likely preparing a massive attack. Following the strikes, he said Ukraine's ability to protect its people depended on its allies willingness to provide more air defence missiles.The appeal came as Zelenskyy returned from the United States, where he said President Donald Trump had agreed to provide Ukraine with licences for Patriot missile systems."It is important that our partners fully understand what is happening and that the protection of people's lives depends directly on their willingness, or lack of willingness, to provide air defence ​missiles," Zelenskyy wrote on Telegram.Poland, a member of the European Union and Nato that shares a border with Ukraine, scrambled fighter jets and activated its air defence network as a precaution following the Russian missile strikes.In a post on X, the Polish armed forces said fighter aircraft and an airborne early warning aircraft had been deployed, while ground-based air defence and radar reconnaissance systems were placed on the highest state of readiness to safeguard the country's airspace. The military said the measures were preventive in nature.Ukraine's long-range drone campaign continued to target Russia's logistics infrastructure, with a warehouse belonging to the country's largest online retailer, Wildberries, catching fire in the western city of Penza.Regional Governor Oleg Melnichenko said one person was injured and around 200 people were evacuated after the attack. The incident came just a day after Wildberries was forced to evacuate another facility in central Russia following a separate Ukrainian drone strike.Following the latest attack, Wildberries said it had rerouted its supply chains to minimise disruptions. The company has increasingly become a target of Ukrainian drone strikes, which have repeatedly hit its warehouse network across Russia.According to the company and local authorities, nearly a dozen Wildberries warehouses have been damaged in recent attacks, destroying about 10% of its storage capacity and causing losses for tens of thousands of small businesses that rely on the platform.The repeated disruptions have also affected ordinary Russians, many of whom depend on online retail as a primary source of income, while Ukraine's campaign against energy facilities, refineries and logistics infrastructure continues to strain Russia's economy.The financial impact is also being felt in the banking sector. Russia's largest lender, Sberbank, has warned that it may need to increase loan-loss provisions as the sustained attacks on Wildberries weigh on the finances of online retailers and their suppliers.
Article Summary: Poland scrambled fighter jets and activated its air defence network as a precaution following the russian missile strikes. Ukraine's long-range drone campaign continued to target russia's logistics infrastructure, with a warehouse belonging to the country's largest online retailer, wildberries, catching fire in penza.

Article Title: Getting 'carried away' again? Musk's million-dollar plan to rescue Trump in mid-elections
Article Text:
Musk’s massive push

‘Got carried away’ in 2024

Days after Elon Musk admitted that he “got carried away” during Donald Trump’s 2024 election campaign, he is once again stepping into the US political arena with a major push to help Republicans win the 2026 midterm elections. The tech billionaire is reviving his political action committee, America PAC, which played a key role in then-presidential candidate Donald Trump’s 2024 campaign.During the 2024 presidential elections, America PAC spent more than $260 million to help Trump secure a win. This time, the group will focus on increasing Republican voter turnout through door-to-door campaigns, digital advertisements and direct mail.Sources familiar with the plans told Axios that the group will target conservative voters, including those who usually do not vote in non-presidential elections.Though the amount the tech mogul plans to spend has not been revealed yet, it is expected to be large considering his spending during the 2024 election.Musk’s donations through America PAC in 2024 made him the biggest individual political donor in a single US election cycle.The group has said that it knocked on more than 10 million doors across more than six swing states during the campaign.For the 2026 midterms, America PAC will work with other Republican groups.By focusing on voter turnout, Musk’s group will allow other Republican organisations to spend more time and money on television advertisements.The campaign will be led by Musk’s top political adviser, Chris Young.“America PAC was an essential partner for our historic GOTV operation in 2024, and their return for 2026 is a huge boost for Republicans across the country,” James Blair, President Trump's senior political adviser, told Axios.“We will again outsmart our opponents and ruthlessly execute our mission for the GOP between now and Election Day,” Blair added.Musk’s return comes at a time when Republicans have a strong financial advantage over Democrats before the November 3 elections. Republican super PACs and committees have a more than $300 million advantage over Democratic groups and $400 million available in Trump’s MAGA Inc. super PAC.The Republican Party hopes this financial strength will help it overcome concerns around Trump’s low approval ratings, especially on the economy and the Iran war.These concerns have created challenges for Republicans as they try to maintain control of the House and possibly the Senate.Musk has been in talks with Trump’s team about how he can support the Republican campaign.“The president's political team and the rest of the GOP apparatus have built a top-notch operation that will put Republicans in a strong position to buck history and retain control of Congress this fall, and we're excited to again be part of the team,” America PAC spokesperson Andrew Romeo told Axios.Musk’s return to political activity comes days after he admitted that he became too involved in politics during his close relationship with Trump. In an interview with The Economist, the entrepreneur said that he should have spent more time running his companies instead of leading the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE).DOGE was a government cost-cutting initiative that oversaw spending cuts and layoffs across government departments. Talking about his political involvement, Musk said, “I got carried away, frankly.”Musk had supported Trump’s 2024 campaign with around $200 million before becoming the head of DOGE.He later admitted that he could have focused more on his businesses. Earlier, during a podcast appearance in December, he had said, “I think instead of doing DOGE, I would have basically worked on my companies,” he had said.Musk’s relationship with Trump became strained after his four-month role leading DOGE. Musk criticised the large spending in Trump’s “big, beautiful bill” and even suggested creating a third party to challenge Republicans.However, his relationship with Trump improved over the following year. By the end of 2025, Musk was again contributing to Republican campaigns.He also donated $10 million to Kentucky GOP Senate candidate Nate Morris, who later left the race to take a job in the Trump administration.
Article Summary: Elon musk is reviving his political action committee, america pac. The group played a key role in then-presidential candidate donald trump’s 2024 campaign. America pac spent more than $260 million to help trump secure a win. It will focus on increasing republican voter turnout through door-to-door campaigns, digital advertisements and direct mail.

Article Title: Watch: US launches 'surprise attack' across Iran targeting IRGC facilities
Article Text:
US forces carried out a large-scale wave of strikes against targets in Iran

The US Central Command (CENTCOM) on Thursday said its forces carried out a large-scale wave of strikes against targets in Iran in response to what it described as attempted missile attacks on US forces a day earlier.According to CENTCOM, the operation targeted dozens of Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) facilities in a "surprise attack" that included military command centres, missile and drone sites, coastal surveillance and defence installations, and maritime capabilities."CENTCOM assets struck dozens of Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) targets ‌in Iran, including military command centers, missile and drone facilities, coastal surveillance and defense sites, and maritime capabilities," the US Central ⁠Command said in a statement.The strikes came hours after US President Donald Trump vowed to respond "very hard" following Iran's reported missile attack on a military base in Jordan hosting US troops.Iranian state media reported that two people were injured in strikes on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz. Explosions were also reported in Khuzestan province in the country's southwest.Elsewhere, drone strikes triggered fires on two natural gas vessels at Egypt's Damietta Port, according to British maritime security firm Ambrey.The vessels included a US-owned floating storage facility and a Greek-owned tanker. The source of the attacks was not immediately known, and no injuries were reported.The fresh attacks on multiple fronts, following several days of relative calm, have heightened fears of a renewed escalation in the conflict. They also highlight the challenges of de-escalating the five-month-long war, which has disrupted global trade and rattled the world economy.Before the latest escalation, mediators had expressed optimism about bringing the United States and Iran back to the negotiating table.However, efforts to revive talks faltered in recent weeks as fighting resumed in the Strait of Hormuz, a vital global energy shipping route that has once again been effectively closed due to Iranian attacks.
Article Summary: Us central command (centcom) said its forces carried out a large-scale wave of strikes against targets in iran. Strikes came hours after us president donald trump vowed to respond "very hard" following iran's reported missile attack on a military base in jordan.

What happens if you miss the July 31, 2026 deadline?

When filing after July 31, 2026 you can only file your return under the new tax regime. So if you plan to opt for the old regime, the deadline assumes more significance for you. The earlier you file the faster your refund, if any will be processed. Filing after the due date may invite unwanted scrutiny which could delay the process and your refund. One major drawback of late filing is that taxpayers cannot carry forward losses, except losses from house property, to future years. A belated income tax return can be filed within nine months from the end of the relevant tax year. So it is by December 31, 2026, for FY 2025-26. But you have to pay a late filing fee of up to Rs 5,000. For taxpayers whose income is below Rs 5 lakh, the fee is capped at Rs 1,000. However, any unpaid tax at your end will attract penal interest at 1% per month from the original due date until the return is filed. Interest on any default in the payment of advance tax will also continue to accrue.

Missed ITR deadline? Here's what happens

It’s the last week of July and like every year the income tax return filing deadline is nearing. For salaried taxpayers July 31, 2026 is the last date on which they can file their ITR within the due date.Taxpayers who earn income from business or profession have a longer window to file their returns. The due date is August 31, 2026, for non-audit cases and October 31, 2026, for cases that require an audit.The process to file the income tax return has evolved over the last few years and the income tax portal now pre-fills a lot of your tax related information drawing from information in documents such as Form 16, Form 26AS, Annual Information Statement (AIS), bank records etc.Yet the onus of the accuracy rests with you, and hence filing your ITR needs to be a careful process to avoid triggering any unwanted scrutiny or queries from the Income Tax department.Before you sit down to file your income tax return, gather all the concerned documents.“The old and new regimes reward very different profiles, and the only reliable way to choose is to compute your liability under both and file under whichever leaves you paying less.Treat this as a calculation, not an instinct,” says CA Chandni Anandan, Tax Expert at ClearTax.When claiming deductions and exemptions it is always wise to keep your records complete and handy. This documentation should stay with you at least till your tax return is processed so that in case of any queries from the department, you have all the information and proofs ready.Log in to the income tax portal (incometax.gov.in/iec/foportal/) using your PAN as the user ID.On the "File your return for the year ended 31-Mar-2026" card, select File Now. If you have a saved draft, choose Resume Filing instead.Select the Assessment Year 2026-27, which corresponds to income that you have earned in the financial year 2025-26.Choose the online mode for a straightforward return. Where your income is more, the offline utility gives you more room to work, after which you upload the generated JSON file to the portal. The online route is the one described here.Select your status as Individual, HUF, or other, as applicable.Choose the return form suited to your income. Many salaried taxpayers file ITR-1, but the right form depends entirely on the nature and mix of your income, so select the one that genuinely fits rather than the one that looks simplest. Please note that if your capital gains from sale of shares etc. does not exceed Rs 1.25 lakh (above which the gains are taxable), then ITR-1 is applicable for you.Verify your personal details and select your income tax regime. To move out of the default new regime, choose Yes against the option to opt out under Section 115BAC(6). This in-return choice is available to those without business or professional income; if you earn such income, opting out requires filing Form 10-IEA separately. While here, confirm your bank details and nominate an account for any refund.Examine the pre-filled income drawn from your Form 16 and from entities that report to the department. Check each figure against your own records, add any income that has not been captured, and claim every deduction you are entitled to. In the case of the new income tax regime, the number of deductions are few, but for those opting for the old regime the list could include medical insurance premium, fixed deposits, HRA or housing loan benefit, Leave Travel Allowance, Section 80C etc.Review the taxes that have already been paid on your behalf, TDS and advance tax. All of these appear pre-filled - confirm the figures and the resulting liability.Proceed to verification and study the tax summary that the income tax portal presents.Preview the return in full, satisfy yourself that it is correct, and only then click on submit.Complete the declaration and proceed to validate your income tax return.If the portal identifies any defects, resolve them before moving on. They are far cheaper to fix now than after filing.If a balance of tax is payable, the sound practice is to pay it before you file so the income tax return goes in fully settled. Filing itself is not conditional on payment, but clearing the dues at this stage spares you interest and a second round of follow-up from the department.Complete e-verification within 30 days, using whichever mode suits you. This step matters more than its placement suggests: the department begins processing only once the return is verified, so verifying promptly is what actually sets your refund and assessment in motion. There are several online options available for verification including Aadhaar-based OTP method which makes the process seamless.But, let’s say you miss the July 31, 2026 deadline. There are several consequences, though filing a belated tax return is still possible.Finance Act, 2026 provides greater flexibility by allowing taxpayers to revise both original and belated income tax returns within 12 months from the end of the relevant tax year.For tax year 2025-26, this means a revised return can be filed up to March 31, 2027, on payment of the applicable fee of Rs 5,000 or Rs 1,000.Even if a taxpayer misses the deadline for filing a belated return, or wants to make changes after submitting a return, there is still an option to file an Updated Income Tax Return (ITR-U) by paying the prescribed additional tax.
Article Summary: Filing your itr needs to be a careful process to avoid triggering any unwanted scrutiny. Filing after the due date may invite unwanted scrutiny which could delay the process and your refund. A belated income tax return can be filed within nine months from the end of the relevant tax year.
